title: BlueQuartz implementation kickoff and runtime intake
next_steps: Redwood to share VPC/network diagram + peering checklist
Customer to provide sample workload trace and 10 representative prompts
Schedule a performance baseline run with Eli (SE) in the staging cluster week of Jan 18
Redwood to send draft SOW and onboarding timeline
action_items: Ana Gutierrez: Share current compliance matrix and SOC2 scoping doc (due: 2027-01-13)
Samir Khatri: Export 24h p95 latency distribution and token distribution, upload to shared folder (due: 2027-01-12)
Eli Voss (Redwood SE): Run quick model compatibility check and list required quantization profile options (due: 2027-01-11)
Maya Chen (Redwood AE): Send SOW draft and billing/contact flow for procurement (due: 2027-01-10)
header:
Date: 2027-01-08
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE); Rajan Patel (Redwood CSM); Eli Voss (Redwood SE); Julia Meyer (BlueQuartz Head of ML Ops); Samir Khatri (BlueQuartz Platform Eng); Ana Gutierrez (BlueQuartz Security); Leo Park (BlueQuartz CTO)
summary: Kickoff to align BlueQuartz implementation plan for Redwood Inference. Covered deployment shape (private VPC vs Dedicated), baseline perf expectations, security/compliance checklist, data residency, and next steps for POC staging. Action items assigned for network artifacts, workload traces, SOC2 scope, and an upcoming performance baseline run.
topics: Deployment options: Private VPC vs Dedicated capacity
Security: SOC2 scope, SSO, KMS, audit logs
Integration touching data residency and network peering
questions: Can we do an air-gapped proof for a subset of inference?
What's the expected p95 latency target for our use case?
How will token-level billing appear on invoices?
What controls exist for KV cache and prefix caching for compliance-sensitive prompts?
transcript: [00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everybody, thanks for joining. I'm Maya from Redwood, I'm the AE on this engagement. Quick roll call?
[00:07] Julia Meyer: Hi this is Julia, head of ML Ops at BlueQuartz. Thanks, excited to get this started.
[00:11] Leo Park: Leo here, CTO. I'll chime in on architecture / timelines.
[00:15] Samir Khatri: Samir, platform engineering, I'll own the network part.
[00:18] Ana Gutierrez: Ana, security. I'll drive compliance and audit asks.
[00:22] Rajan Patel: Rajan from Redwood CSM, I'll partner on onboarding milestones.
[00:25] Eli Voss: Eli, SE — I'll lead the perf tests and staging runs.

[00:30] Maya Chen: Awesome. Goal for today: agree on the onboarding runway, capture blockers, and assign immediate next steps so we can start the staging baseline. We'll keep it to an hour and leave overflow for follow-ups. Sound good?

[00:40] Julia Meyer: Yep. Our timeline is kinda tight — we want a limited internal pilot by end of Q1. So ideally a two-week staging run then a short pilot ramp. We also need to validate no PII leaves our VPC — so private deployment or VPC peering is a must.

[00:55] Maya Chen: Totally understood. We support Private with customer-managed VPC or Dedicated for isolated capacity. Rajan, can you quickly talk through typical timelines for a Private on-prem/VPC onboarding?

[01:05] Rajan Patel: Sure. For Private VPC, once we have the network diagram and peering details it's usually 7-10 business days to provision the control plane and coordinate the peering tests, then another week to validate workloads. If you want on-prem air-gap that adds coordination — there's a separate package and extra security review but we've done it for a handful of customers.

[01:25] Ana Gutierrez: When you say "we've done it," is that a full air-gapped bundle or just an approved VPC pattern? We have strict audit requirements and need assurance on KMS and HSM integration, plus audit logs retained for 12 months.

[01:40] Eli Voss: We support KMS integration and can talk to HSM via customer-managed keys. Audit logs can be exported to your SIEM — retention windows are configurable based on the enterprise package. For true air-gapped on-prem, we ship an appliance package and a control-plane handshake when permitted — that process has compliance gating and longer lead time.
[02:05] Ana Gutierrez: Okay, can you share the SOC2 scope and what artifacts you need from us to complete onboarding?

[02:12] Maya Chen: We'll share a SOC2 scoping checklist. Action item: Ana to share your compliance matrix and any additional controls — we'll map them to our standard. We'll also share a redwood security packet and reference SAML/SSO instructions.

[02:25] Samir Khatri: On the network side, we need the exact CIDR ranges, whether we'll allow cross-account peering, and expected egress patterns. Also curious about NAT and egress through your endpoints — any special port requirements for the runtime?

[02:40] Eli Voss: Ports are standard — outbound TLS to specific endpoints for control plane. For the inference nodes, if you're using Private with dedicated GPUs, traffic stays in your VPC after peering. I'll email the minimal firewall rules; Samir, if you can provide the diagram we'll run a preflight check.

[02:55] Julia Meyer: Perf wise, our main KPI is p95 < 350 ms for single-turn generation at 512 tokens for the assist workflow. We can tolerate higher for batch offline. Cost is also a big factor; we want guidance on batching and quantization tradeoffs.

[03:15] Eli Voss: p95 350ms at 512 tokens is doable depending on model family and hardware. We'll need your sample prompt set and the token distribution to recommend quantization profile and batching settings. For low-latency SLOs we might advise smaller batch windows and prefix caching. For cost savings, quantize to int8 or int4 depending on accuracy loss. I'll run a compatibility check based on your model.
[03:35] Julia Meyer: We're evaluating a fine-tuned LlamaX variant. Any known issues there?

[03:40] Eli Voss: LlamaX family is supported, but the fine-tune format matters — we sometimes see tokenization mismatches around custom special tokens. We'll ask for a small model artifact and a handful of prompts. Compatibility check is an early action item.
[03:55] Leo Park: Regarding data residency — our EMEA customers require EU-only data processing. How does Redwood handle region pinning?

[04:05] Maya Chen: We have region controls and routing policies. For Private you can select region and we can ensure no cross-region fallback. For hosted, we route by geo but you should assume logs may travel unless you choose private with explicit region constraints. We'll add a note to the compliance mapping.
[04:20] Samir Khatri: What about token-level billing visibility? We need to map chargeback to internal teams.

[04:26] Rajan Patel: The Console provides token-level breakdown per route and model. We can set up per-team API keys, usage dashboards, and monthly export to your billing system. We'll send a sample export format.
[04:40] Ana Gutierrez: We also need RBAC and SSO — we use Azure AD with SCIM provisioning. Any blockers?
[04:48] Eli Voss: No blockers. We support SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning; we'll share the SSO doc. For RBAC you can map roles to API keys and have scoped permissions.
[05:00] Julia Meyer: For the POC, we want a baseline run in staging with 24-hour synthetic traffic that mirrors production load. Can Redwood help run that?

[05:08] Eli Voss: Yes, we'll coordinate. If you provide the token distribution and the 10 canonical prompts, we can drive a 24-hour p95/p50/p99 comparison and KV cache hit-rate measurements. We'll also surface model regression signals so you can check quality tradeoffs when using quantized models.
[05:26] Samir Khatri: One thing: our infra team is wary of automatic KV caching because some prompts include transient identifiers. How is cache invalidation handled?

[05:36] Eli Voss: Cache is configurable. You can disable prefix/KV caching per route, set TTLs, and we provide audit of cache hits. For compliance-sensitive routes you can mark them no-cache. We'll demonstrate this in the runbook.

[05:50] Rajan Patel: Quick note: we'll propose a two-sprint onboarding plan. Sprint 0 — network and compliance preflight. Sprint 1 — staging baseline and integration. We'll send a proposed timeline after today's call.
[05:58] Julia Meyer: Sounds good. Any procurement/contract concerns? Leo?
[06:02] Leo Park: Procurement will need SOW, pricing, and standard security appendices. We also need clarity on data retention and liability around model outputs. Is that covered in the SOW?

[06:12] Maya Chen: We'll include data retention, logging retention, SLA specifics in the SOW. Maya to send initial draft today or tomorrow — action item. Also we'll include a standard acceptable use and liability section and flag any items for legal review.
[06:25] Ana Gutierrez: On logging, do you provide immutable audit logs? We need evidence trails for admin actions and API key usage.
[06:32] Eli Voss: Yes, audit logs include admin console actions and token-level usage anchors. They can be exported to your logging endpoint.
[06:40] Julia Meyer: For the performance run, we'd like the SE to run two variants: 1) highest-performance unquantized and 2) cost-optimized quantized. Then we can evaluate quality delta.
[06:52] Eli Voss: That's standard. I'll prepare a comparison matrix and suggest quantization knobs. We'll also run a small quality eval against your golden prompts.
[07:02] Samir Khatri: Networking — what's the small firewall rule set? We can't open many egress ports.

[07:08] Eli Voss: Minimal egress over TLS to control-plane endpoints plus health checks. I'll put the exact ports in the preflight doc. If you prefer strictly isolated flow we can use a peering model with no public egress.
[07:20] Julia Meyer: Great. Anything else we should capture?

[07:24] Maya Chen: I want to capture risks: lead time for air-gapped on-prem could add 4-6 weeks; SOC2 mapping may surface 3rd-party log shipping concerns; model compatibility could require tokenization tweaks. We'll capture those in the onboarding risk log.
[07:40] Leo Park: Acceptable. On headcount, who's owning the staging run on your side?
[07:44] Julia Meyer: I'll own with Samir doing network, Ana for security. We'll loop in procurement when SOW lands.

[07:52] Maya Chen: Perfect. To recap action items — Ana shares compliance artifacts; Samir provides network diagram and token distributions; Eli will run compatibility checks and seed the staging perf plan; Maya sends SOW and timeline. We'll schedule the baseline run week of Jan 18. Any objections?
[08:10] Ana Gutierrez: No objections. Please include the SCIM/SSO docs in the packet.
[08:16] Rajan Patel: Noted — I'll attach SSO/SCIM and sample billing export in the follow-up email.
[08:22] Julia Meyer: One micro thing: can we get a short runbook for incident escalation and support SLAs?
[08:28] Rajan Patel: Yes — we'll include the support contacts, escalation matrix, and SLA targets in the playbook.
[08:35] Eli Voss: I'll also add a small checklist for cache controls and per-route settings for the POC.

[08:40] Maya Chen: Great. We'll send notes and the SOW by EOD tomorrow, aim to have the preflight artifacts in by Jan 12 so the SE can run checks before Jan 18. Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with calendar invites for the baseline window.
[08:50] Julia Meyer: Thanks all, talk soon.
[08:55] Leo Park: Thanks.
